description: Clip dim ROW contract. `clips[i].raw["dim"]` is the share of the way to black the device draws a clip's picture at: 0.01..1 in hundredths, each encoded pixel times 1 - dim. Python (app.kria.clip_dim) and Swift (ClipDim) must each turn every `valid` value into `normalized` (null = the key is omitted from the row and the recipe clip has no `dim`), and reject every `invalid` value. One rule on both sides, in IEEE doubles: a value below 0 is invalid (-0.0 is not below 0); a value below 0.01 is no dim; anything else rounds half up to hundredths as floor(dim * 100 + 0.5) / 100, and a result above 1 is invalid. So 0.125 is 0.13, 0.005 is no dim and 1.004 is black. 0.285 * 100 + 0.5 is 28.999999999999996 in doubles, so 0.285 rounds down to 0.28. A percent (40) is not a strength.
